chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, who said:
Some of my family narrated to me that a young man came to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام and confessed before him to theft.

He said: So he عليه السلام said to him, "I see you are a young man and there is no harm in your appearance; do you recite anything from the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes, Surat al-Baqarah." He said: "Then I have granted your hand for Surat al-Baqarah."
He said: He only refrained from cutting him because no clear proof had been established against him.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, the title of Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, mentioned in relation to the young man’s recitation
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: legal proof or evidentiary proof required for enforcement
key_terms.بِالسَّرِقَةِ: for theft; the confessed offense in the report
key_terms.سُورَةَ الْبَقَرَةِ: Surat al-Baqarah, the surah the young man said he recited
key_terms.وَهَبْتُ يَدَكَ: I have granted your hand; an expression indicating that the hand was not cut

ai.seo_question: Why did Amir al-Mu'minin Ali عليه السلام not cut the hand of a man who confessed to theft?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that a young man confessed to theft before Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, who engaged him concerning his recitation of the Qur'an and then did not carry out the amputation. The report concludes by clarifying that the punishment was not enforced because legal proof had not been established against him. It highlights the importance of evidentiary standards in judicial rulings.
